FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Hydraulic Structures Instrumentation Sectional Committee had been approved by the Water Resources Division 
Council. 


Foundation settlement (baseplate) apparatus are installed on the foundation under dams and embankments to 
permit measurements of vertical settlement of the foundation during construction and later during operation. This 
type of apparatus generally is used where the height of the dam or embankment is relatively low and where the 
foundation is unconsolidated sand, silt, or clay material. This installation is similar to the cross arm installation 
for measurement of internal vertical movement in earth dams (see IS 7500 : 2000 “Code of practice for installation 
and observation of cross arms for measurement of internal vertical movement in earth dams (First Revision )’). 
For the choice and location of instruments in earth dams, reference may be made to IS 7436 (Part 1) : 1993 “Guide 
for Types of Measurements for Structures in River Valley Projects and Criteria for Choice and Location Of 
Measuring instruments Part | For Earth and Rockfill Dams (First Revision)”. An electrical probe with PVC 
casing pipe as described in IS 7500 may also be used for the baseplate installation. The pipe system installed for 
the baseplate system can be usefully utilized for measurement of the water level, if any, at that point. 


In the formulation of this standard due weightage has been given to international coordination among the standards 
and practices prevailing in different countries in addition to relating it to the practices prevailing in this field in 
this country. 


This standard was first published in 1976; however, the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard 
decided to revise it based on the experience gained since then as well as considering technological development 
in the field. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 
‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)’. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off 
value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 8226 : 2017 


Indian Standard 


INSTALLATION AND OBSERVATION OF BASE 
PLATE APPARATUS FOR MEASUREMENT 
OF FOUNDATION SETTLEMENT IN 
EMBANKMENTS — CODE OF PRACTICE 


(First Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


This standard lays down details of installation and 
observation of baseplate apparatus for observing 
foundation settlement of dams and embankments 
resting on soil strata. For the purpose of this standard 
the word embankment includes earth and rock-fill dams. 


2 REFERENCES 


The following standards contain provisions, which 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions of 
this standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to 
revision, and parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards 
indicated below:

3 EQUIPMENT 


7436 (Part 1): 
1993 


3.1 Components of Installation 


3.1.1 The foundation settlement apparatus consists of 
a baseplate placed on the foundation excavation line 
and a vertical column of steel pipes (see Fig. 1). The 
apparatus comprises a base section of 50 mm steel pipe, 
a cross arm measuring unit (baseplate), and anchor 
crossarm and an extension of 50 mm pipes to the surface 
of the embankment. 


3.1.2 Base Section 


The base section is made of two pieces of 50 mm pipe, 


one 600 mm long and one | 500 mm long, joined by a 
pipe coupling. A latching plate (see Fig. 2) having 4 
drill holes of 18 mm diameter is inserted into the 
coupling between these two sections of pipes. 


3.1.3 Baseplate 


The baseplate is a modified crossarm with two 300 x 
375 mm steel plates of 5 mm thickness welded to the 
base of 1 000 mm length of 75 mm channel section. 
The base-plate unit is bolted and welded to a 40 mm 
pipe which telescopes between lengths of 50 mm pipe 
in the system. Settlement readings are taken only on 
the baseplate measuring point which is the bottom of 
the 40 mm pipe. 


3.1.4 Anchor Crossarm 


At 1 150 mm above the elevation of the baseplate, an 
anchor crossarm is placed to prevent the vertical pipe 
column from sliding down on the baseplate. The anchor 
crossarm is a 1 000 mm length of 75 mm channel, bolted 
and welded to a 1 500 mm length of 50 mm pipe. 


3.1.5 Extension Pipe 


To complete the installation, 1 500 mm lengths of 50 
mm pipe are joined by pipe couplings to extend the 
column of pipes to the surface of the embankment. 


3.2 Equipment for Observation 
3.2.1 Measuring Torpedo (see Fig. 3) 


Readings of baseplate are taken by lowering from the 
top of the system a torpedo attached to a steel measuring 
tape. The torpedo is machined to dimensions from a 
brass shaft and contains two wings or pawls, which open 
or close at opening slots and closing slots due to spring 
action. The maximum dimension of torpedo is at the 
wings when fully opened and this dimension is less than 
50 mm and greater than 40 mm. 


3.2.2 Reading Scale and Adapter 


The details of reading scale with adapter used for 
lowering the torpedo are given in Fig. 4.

4 INSTALLATION 


4.1 Prior to installation of the test equipment, permanent 
instrument benchmarks and targets shall be established 
beyond the area of influence of reservoir and/or 
embankment load. These targets shall be visible and 
accessible throughout construction of the entire 
embankment. These targets and benchmarks are utilized 
to locate the centre of the installation at all stages of 
construction. 


4.2 Base Extension (see Fig. 5A and 6A) 


The centre of installation should be located and level 


area of at least 900 mm dia adjacent to centre line of 
installation at foundation line. A trench should be 
excavated up to 500 mm below foundation line as 
shown in the Fig. 5A. The base extension for the device 
consists of two pieces of pipe which form, the extension 
into the foundation. This extension should be assembled 
and set into a 100 mm minimum diameter hole which 
has been drilled to the required depth into the 
foundation. The hole may be drilled by an earth auger. 
After placement of the pipe extension, the backfill 
around the 50 mm pipe should be done with sand and 
cement grout. If the foundation baseplate is not installed 
immediately, a temporary removable pipe cover should

be placed over the extending 50 mm pipe and backfill 
with fine soil up to foundation line. Thereafter, compact 
embankment (450 mm minimum) above installation. 


4.3 The foundation settlement apparatus shall be 
installed as embankment placement operations 
progress. Each pipe section shall be placed in a vertical 
position. The operation of all heavy equipment should 
be prohibited in the immediate vicinity of the 
installation when sections of the apparatus are being 
placed. If, for some reason, the upper surface of the 
embankment in the vicinity of the installation is to be 
reworked before an additional extension pipe is placed, 
the installation shall be flagged or marked so that it 
will not be damaged or displaced by earth moving 
equipment. 


4.4 Installation in Rock-free Soils 
4.4.1 Baseplate (See Fig. 5B) 


The centre of installation should be located and a trench 
excavated up to foundation excavation line. The soil 
above pipe cover of the base extension should be 


removed and the pipe cover also be removed. The 
baseplate unit should be placed and aligned over the 
base extension. A pipe cover should be placed on top 
of the 40 mm pipe of the baseplate unit and the joints 
of the 40 mm pipe with the base extension pipe at 
bottom should be fitted with oakum wrapped with 
burlap. The trench should be backfilled with 
embankment material to the level of pipe cover at top. 
The original elevation of the baseplate should be noted 
by lowering the torpedo in the pipe by removing the 
temporary pipe cover as described in 5.1 and the pipe 
cover replaced. The compacted backfilling should then 
be continued up to the original embankment level. 
Embankment placement should then be continued. 


4.4.2 Extension Pipe and Anchor Crossarm 
(See Fig. 5C) 


The centre of the installation should be located and 
excavate a trench up to bottom of anchor crossarm. A 
200 mm diameter hole should be bored from the bottom 
of the trench so as to locate the pipe cover placed in 
operation described in 4.4.1. Remove soil up to 325

mm below top of 40 mm pipe cover as shown. The 
pipe cover should be removed and the 50 mm pipe with 
anchor crossarm placed and aligned over the baseplate 
unit. A pipe cover should be placed on top of the 50 
mm pipe and the joints of the 50 mm pipe with the 
baseplate unit at bottom should be fitted with oakum 
wrapped with burlap. The trench and borehole should 
be backfilled with embankment material to the level of 
pipe cover at top. The elevation of the baseplate should 
be noted by lowering the torpedo in the pipe by 
removing the temporary pipe cover as described in 4.1 
and the pipe cover replaced. The compacted backfilling 
should then be continued up to the original embankment 
level. Embankment placement should then be 
continued. 


4.4.3 Extension of Pipe to Top of Embankment 


For each extension pipe, the operations are similar to 
those described in 4.4.2 except that no trench is required 
to be excavated as no cross-arms are installed at higher 
levels. However cross-arms may be installed at higher 
elevations so that it becomes a combined foundation 


settlement and vertical movement device (see IS 7500). 
The extension pipes should be placed by using 50 mm 
pipe couplings till the surface of the embankment is 
reached. At the surface of the embankment, rocky 
material should be placed around the pipe extension 
and concrete placed above so as to afford fixity to the 
installation (see Fig. 5D). At the top of the last 50 mm 
pipe a plug should be fitted to a 50 mm coupling. 


4.5 Installation in Rocky Materials 


4.5.1 It is difficult to bore a hole in rocky material. The 
operations involved in the installation as described 
in 4.4.1 to 4.4.3 are therefore modified. The pipe cover 
over the base extension, if placed should be removed 
and the baseplate unit should be placed and aligned 
over the base extension. A pipe cover should be placed 
on top of the 40 mm pipe of the baseplate unit and the 
joints of the 40-mm pipe with the base extension pipe 
at bottom should be fitted with oakum wrapped with 
burlap. Backfilling should be done to 250 mm above 
the centre line of baseplate. At this stage, the pipe cover 
should be removed and the original elevation of

Operations: 

1. Locate centre of installation. 

2. Level 900 mm dia area adjacent to centre of installation at foundation line. 

3. Excavate a trench 500 mm below foundation line as shown. 

4. Bore 100 mm minimum dia hole; clean hole. 

5. Place and align foundation extension in borehole. 

6. Place a removable pipe cover. 

7. Place sand-cement grout around pipe, preferably with a tremie, tamp fine soil around cover to foundation line. 
8. Compact embankment above installation.

baseplate measuring point should be obtained. Then 
the extension pipe with anchor cross-arm should be

the baseplate unit at bottom should be fitted with oakum 
wrapped with burlap. A mound of rocky material should 
be placed around the baseplate pipe and extension pipe 
to about 75 mm below the pipe cover at the top to 
support the pipe. The embankment placement around 
the pipe should be continued till it reaches a level of 
150 mm above the pipe cover, leaving a depression 
around the pipe cover (see Fig. 6B). After the anchor 
cross-arm unit is thus installed, the protective pipe cover 
should be removed and the vertical alignment of the 


system should be checked by lowering a plumb bob. If 
any deviation from vertical alignment is found, an 
attempt should be made immediately to correct the 
error. If it is impracticable to correct the error, 
succeeding pipe sections should be placed vertically 
and the offset from the true vertical alignment should 
be recorded. Succeeding extension pipes should be 
placed similarly by using 50 mm pipe couplings (see 
Fig. 6C) till the surface of the embankment is reached. 
At the surface of the embankment, rocky soil should 
be placed around the pipe extension and concrete 
should be placed above so as to afford fixity to the 
installation (see Fig. 6D). At the top of the last 50 mm 
pipe a plug should be fitted to a 50 mm coupling.

5 OBSERVATIONS 


5.1 Settlement readings shall be taken on the baseplate 
measuring point which is the bottom of the 40 mm pipe 
by means of the measuring torpedo shown in Fig. 3. 
The elevation of the measuring point of the baseplate 
is determined by lowering the torpedo through the 
reading scale and into the pipe system by means of the 
steel tape. Pawls on the torpedo engage the lower end 
of the 40 mm pipe (the measuring point), and upon 
reaching the bottom of the installation and striking the 
latching plate, they latch in a closed position to enable 
the torpedo to be withdrawn from the system. When 
readings are made, the reading scale is attached to the 
top section of the pipe projecting from the existing 
installation. The elevation of the levelling plate on top 
of the reading scale shall be established from a 
permanent benchmark of the embankment. 


5.2 During construction, readings for elevations of the 
baseplate measuring points and of the top of the 
embankment should be determined and noted in the 


form given in Annex A. Throughout construction, 
including shut-downs, readings shall be taken at 
intervals of 30 day. When the installation is completed 
the elevation of the top of the final pipe coupling should 
be established to the nearest 5 mm (see Note) and the 
date of completion should be noted on the form shown 
in Annex A. The first set of periodic readings should 
be made immediately after installation; thereafter 
readings should be taken every 3 months for the first 3 
years and every 6 months thereafter. The observations 
should be recorded in the form given in Annex A. 


NOTE — The elevation of the final pipe coupling shall be 
verified at least once in 6 months with a permanent benchmark. 


6 RECORD TESTS 


Record tests of foundation materials at the instrument 
installation are necessary. Representative undisturbed 
samples of the foundation soils should be obtained and 
tested for grain size analysis, consistency limits, specific 
gravity, natural water content, natural dry density and 
consolidation.

Operations: 

1. Locate centre of installation. 

2. Excavate a trench up to bottom of anchor crossarm. 

3. Bore 200 mm dia hole up to top of 40 mm pipe cover; clean hole. 

4. Remove soil up to 325 mm below top of 40 mm pipe cover as shown. 

5. Remove pipe cover, place and align 50 mm pipe with anchor crossarm over baseplate unit. 

6. Place a removable pipe cover at top of 50 mm pipe. 

7. Wrap with oakum and burlap at joints of the 50 mm pipe with baseplate unit. 

8. Backfill the trench and borehole with embankment up to the pipe cover at top. 

9. Remove pipe cover at top of 50 mm pipe and obtain original elevation of the baseplate measuring point using 
torpedo. 

10. Place a removable pipe cover at top of 50 mm pipe and compacted backfilling is done up to original embankment 
level. 

11. Continue embankment placing. 


Fig. 5 C Phase 3 


Operations: 
Locate centre of installation. 

Bore 200 mm dia hole up to top of 50 mm pipe cover; clean hole. 

Remove pipe cover, connect 50 mm extension pipe using 50 mm dia pipe coupling. 
Place a removable pipe cover at top of 50 mm extension pipe. 

Backfill the borehole with embankment up to the pipe cover at top. 

Remove pipe cover at top of 50 mm pipe and obtain original elevation of the baseplate measuring point using 


torpedo.

Operations: 
1. Locate centre of installation. 


2. Remove soil above pipe cover; remove pipe cover from 
base extension. 


Place and align baseplate unit over base extension. 
Place a removable pipe cover at top of 40 mm pipe. 


Wrap with oakum and burlap at joints of the 40 mm pipe 
with base extension (A); backfill up to 250 mm above 
centre line of baseplate.

torpedo.

shown.

alignment of the system by means of a plumb bob; 
attempt correction of deviation, if any, from vertical.

4. Continue embankment placing to a level 150 mm

Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 


‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards : Monthly Additions’. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: WRD 16 (0588).
